headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: Cursor’s broad filesystem/MCP access can feed Khoj’s retrieval pipeline with untrusted content and sensitive notes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files, clipboard, and use MCP; Khoj reads indexed documents and notes. That creates a plausible default bridge where Cursor-authored or attacker-controlled content can be ingested by Khoj as trusted text. No direct shared channel is documented beyond files, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cursor writes attacker-controlled instructions into files that Khoj indexes, Khoj may surface them as trusted context.
IF the two agents share a local notes/workspace directory, prompt injection becomes reachable without extra tooling.
mitigations: Disable automatic indexing of editor/workspace folders in Khoj.
Keep Cursor and Khoj pointed at separate directories.
Review retrieved snippets before acting on them.
Turn off MCP integrations in Cursor for shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can call cloud or self-hosted servers. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or notes can flow from Cursor into Khoj’s retrieval and then out through Khoj’s backend or search providers, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF Cursor and Khoj share a local filesystem or synced notes folder, sensitive files can be indexed by Khoj.
IF Khoj is configured to use cloud search or a remote server, indexed content may leave the device.
mitigations: Separate code and personal-notes directories.
Exclude secrets and private notes from Khoj indexing.
Use self-hosted Khoj only for sensitive corpora.
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem and modify git state; Khoj can read files and maintains a shared index across clients. They do not both write the same mutable store, but Cursor can change files that Khoj consumes, and concurrent edits can create stale or conflicting state in shared workspaces. The overlap is real but not a direct write-write collision.
conditions: IF Cursor edits files that Khoj indexes while Khoj is refreshing its index, Khoj may serve stale or inconsistent results.
IF both are pointed at the same git working tree, Cursor’s commits can race with Khoj-driven file reads.
mitigations: Avoid sharing a live git working tree with Khoj.
Pause indexing during large Cursor refactors.
Use branch-based workflows for code changes.
Keep Khoj read-only on project directories.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or snapshot indexing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code and file edits; Khoj can retrieve and present those outputs from indexed documents. If Khoj treats Cursor-produced text as authoritative, downstream reasoning can amplify mistakes or hallucinations into notes or decisions. Khoj is not an autonomous action agent here, so the blast radius is limited below high.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieves Cursor-generated notes or code comments without verification, it may propagate errors.
IF a user copies Cursor output into indexed notes, Khoj may later present it as factual.
mitigations: Mark AI-generated notes clearly.
Verify retrieved claims against source files.
Restrict Khoj to curated note collections.
Use explicit review before acting on retrieved content.
requires-engineering: add source-confidence scoring.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or self-hosted servers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in shared indexed content, differing retention and hosting choices can create compliance mismatch. The profiles do not prove a specific residency violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that Khoj indexes and Khoj is configured to use a remote server, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF Cursor clipboard contents include sensitive data, that data can enter indexed notes indirectly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of indexed folders.
Use self-hosted Khoj with strict retention settings.
Disable clipboard-based workflows for sensitive material.
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls.
